title: Constant geometric stalks and point-transport Frobenius are the coefficient unit
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_m=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ for $m\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Y_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Equip the constant finite coefficient sheaves $(A_m)_Y$, their completed integral unit $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, and its rationalization $E_Y$ with the canonical geometric Weil comparisons of [def-weil-constant-weil-structure]: at the integral and rational levels $\theta_{\mathcal O_E}$ and $\theta_E$, and at the finite level $\theta_m=c_m\circ\lambda_m:Lg_Y^*(A_m)_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}(A_m)_Y$, where $c_m$ is the finite-level structure isomorphism of [def-weil-constant-weil-structure] and $\lambda_m$ the identification of the derived pullback along the isomorphism $g_Y$ with the inverse image [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]. Write $g_Y,g_s$ for geometric Galois Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed].

For every $n\ge1$, every $x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ and every geometric point $\bar x:s\to Y$ obtained from an embedding $\mathbf F_{q^n}\hookrightarrow k$, the return is $g_Y^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$. Use the actual point transports $\iota$ of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], their iterates $I^{[n]}$, the specified pullback-composition comparisons, and the iterated canonical Weil maps to form the local operators of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] at finite, integral and rational levels. There are canonical coefficient-unit identifications
$$\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*(A_m)_Y)\simeq A_m[0],\qquad
\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})\simeq\mathcal O_E[0],\qquad
\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*E_Y)\simeq E[0].$$
Under these identifications the composite local operators are respectively $1_{A_m[0]}$, $1_{\mathcal O_E[0]}$ and $1_{E[0]}$. The identifications and operator equalities commute with every reduction $A_{m+1}\to A_m$, the projections of the completed integral unit to the finite levels, and rationalization $-\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi].
